notes: Site is a live Shopify store (francfrancjp.myshopify.com), reached via direct HTTP fetch (curl_cffi/requests, tier 1), no Claude-specific robots.txt disallow. Discovery: full header-menu JSON + footer/category-accordion tree from /pages/category_list, robots.txt (which has an explicit 'Allow: /collections/*ranking/' rule hinting at a ranking taxonomy), sitemap_collections_1/2.xml (3089 collection URLs enumerated), and direct probes of common English candidate handles (best-sellers, bestsellers, best-selling, popular, top-sellers, customer-favorites -> all HTTP 404, none exist). FOUND AND INVESTIGATED: the site has a large 'ranking-<department>' collection family (300+ handles found in sitemap, e.g. ranking-table, ranking-kitchen, ranking-sofa, ranking-bed, ranking-bedding, ranking-cushion_cover, ranking-fragrance, ranking-appliance, ranking-rugmat_carpet, plus a top-level ranking-all) whose page titles/meta all read '[Category] Ranking - Popular Recommendations - Product List' (e.g. ranking-table = 'テーブル ランキング'/'人気おすすめ', matching the target term 'Most Popular'/'Popular Products'). VERIFIED by exhaustive products.json pagination and product-ID-set comparison that this is NOT a distinct curated Bestsellers concept: ranking-table (126 items) and the base 'table' category (126 items) are the IDENTICAL product set (100% ID overlap, 0 unique either side); same result for ranking-kitchen vs 'kitchen' (1724 items, 100% identical). 7 of 9 sampled ranking-<dept> handles matched their base department's qty exactly. ranking-all itself returns 5082 unique products against a store-wide catalogue total of 6297 (verified via /collections/all/products.json exhaustive pagination) = 81% of the entire catalogue sorted by popularity, not a curated top-N bestseller list. Conclusion: 'ranking-*' is a site-wide alternate-sort VIEW of each existing category (and of the whole catalogue for ranking-all), not a genuine distinct Bestsellers merchandising concept -- excluded per brief Sec 3 test #2 ('not just a page that happens to sort by/mention bestselling products'). Also found and excluded: /collections/26firsthalf-hit-ranking ('上半期ヒット ランキング' = 'H1 2026 Hit Ranking', 42 products) -- a genuinely small curated list, but it is a dated, expired seasonal campaign artifact (H1 2026 has already passed; today is 2026-09-09) with zero links from any live nav/header/footer/category tree or homepage (sitemap-only orphan, no sibling period pages found e.g. no 25secondhalf/26secondhalf equivalent), so treated as a stale campaign remnant rather than a current Bestsellers feature. /collections/recommend-items (879 items, 'おすすめアイテム'/'Recommended Items', og:description explicitly 'スタッフもイチ押しの商品' = staff-recommended items) was also checked and excluded: this is editorial staff-curation, not a sales/popularity-based Bestsellers concept, and is not in the brief's target-term list. Navigation checked: header dropdown menus, footer/category accordion tree (/pages/category_list), sitemap_collections (both files, 3089 URLs), and direct probes of English URL-shape candidates. No genuine curated Bestsellers/Top-Sellers/Popular-Products PLP, distinct from an ordinary category or the whole catalogue, was found on this site. Result is rows: [] as a real, checked absence, not a failure to look.
